_about: Direct far JMPs from a movable code segment to a movable segment of the same module. nevalid.py rejects every such jump unless it is listed here with matching target and context bytes. Each entry says why the far return on the stack at that jump is not a CS:IP pushed by hand in the jumping segment. A jump that a push walk proves is reached from a "push cs / push" pair is rejected even if listed. Entries marked provisional have not been fully established and need an independent check.

farjmp.why: tail jump out of the program entry (exported ordinal 100, 1:0000). No PUSH CS between the entry and this jump; the far return on the stack is the one pushed by the application stub's far CALL to ordinal 100.

jump to the runtime error raiser (7:0279..0292, error number in BL/BX). The raiser walks the BP chain to the active error-handler frame and resumes there; it does not RETF to the address on the stack at this jump. Read as far as 7:02E2; the non-return is not proven beyond that.
exported entry thunk (ordinal 691 = 7:05DC is this JMP itself): the far return on the stack is the far caller's.

reached only through the near table at 7:0000 used by "jmp cs:[bx-2]" at 7:008E (exported ordinal 110). Ordinal 110 is entered by the far jumps of the p-code dispatcher in segment 2 (2:496A...), which since 49358e0 go through wrapper stubs, so the far return on the stack here is the wrapper's (FIXED segment), not a CS of segment 7. PROVISIONAL: other far callers of ordinal 110 were not enumerated.
